caption: Average performance of different models on the November 2024 AMC-10 and AMC-12 tests. This is the average score (with maximum score 150) over the four tests on 100 runs with temperature t=0.5. We chose t = 0.5 to follow simple-evals <cit.>. Error bars are 2 of the estimate. On competition math, scores well above its weight-class even compared to non–open-weight models.
model_annotation: The bar chart titled “Average performance on November 2024 AMC 10/12 tests” illustrates average scores for a set of named language models under a fixed sampling temperature, with each bar representing one model’s average score and showing an uncertainty estimate via error bars. The horizontal axis contains the categorical model names, displayed as diagonally rotated labels, ordered left-to-right as: “Llama-3.3 70B Instruct,” “Claude 3.5 Sonnet,” “Qwen 2.5 14b-Instruct,” “GPT 4o,” “GPT 4o-mini,” “Qwen 2.5 72b-Instruct,” “Gemini Flash 1.5,” “Gemini Pro 1.5,” and “phi-4.” The vertical axis is the value axis and is labeled “Average score (temperature = 0.5),” shown on a linear scale with numeric ticks spanning roughly from 60 up to just under 95. A legend in the upper-left indicates two bar colors: light blue for “Large model” and dark blue for “Small model.” From left to right, the bars and their printed values are: Llama-3.3 70B Instruct (light blue) at 66.4; Claude 3.5 Sonnet (light blue) at 74.8; Qwen 2.5 14b-Instruct (dark blue) at 77.4; GPT 4o (light blue) at 77.9; GPT 4o-mini (dark blue) at 78.2; Qwen 2.5 72b-Instruct (light blue) at 78.7; Gemini Flash 1.5 (dark blue) at 81.6; Gemini Pro 1.5 (light blue) at 89.8; and phi-4 (dark blue) at 91.8. Each bar includes a black error bar with caps extending slightly above and below the bar top, and numeric value annotations are placed above each bar; the bars appear arranged in increasing order of the annotated average score, and no bars are otherwise specially shaded or outlined beyond the two-color encoding.
